newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Liberals slip in Manitoba - poll.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Liberals slip in Manitoba - poll.

text.p: Canada's ruling Liberal party has lost some ground in the Western Canadian province of Manitoba ahead of the June 2 federal election, according to a Winnipeg Free Press poll published on Thursday.

A May 21-23 phone survey of 1,004 Manitobans by Probe Research Inc showed Liberal support falling to 35 percent from 36 percent in a May 2-7 poll. The new poll had a 3.1 percent margin of error, 19 times out of 20.
The Liberals, who have a solid lead in national polls, won 12 of Manitoba's 14 seats with 45 percent of the vote in the 1993 election.
But they aroused voter anger in southern Manitoba when Prime Minister Jean Chretien called the election last month one day after surveying damage in the province's worst flooding in 145 years.
Support for the right-wing Reform Party rose to 21 percent in the new poll from 14 percent, but was down from its 22 percent vote in the 1993 election when it won one Manitoba seat.
The left-wing New Democratic Party's backing fell to 23 percent from 28 percent, but the party posed a threat in several electoral districts held by the Liberals, the Free Press said.
The NDP won one seat in Manitoba in 1993 on 17 percent of the vote.
The Conservatives fell to 21 percent from 22 percent in the previous poll. They polled 12 percent in Manitoba in 1993.
The results came after the apportionment of undecided voters.
